mainTopic: Drawn water that disqualifies a מקוה or a טבילה, and the punishments of עדים זוממין
overview: The amud opens with the end of a quoted משנה about three לוגין of drawn water, just short of the full amount, into which a קורטוב of wine or milk fell. The תנא קמא says the מקוה is not disqualified, while רבי יוחנן בן נורי says everything follows the appearance. The גמרא then asks whether רבא can really say that רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, since רב פפא was unsure how רב read the משנה. The answer is that רב פפא had a doubt, but רבא was sure. אביי then reminds רב יוסף that רב יוסף himself once taught the other reading, under which רב's ruling fits everyone. Next comes another ruling of רב: if a barrel of drawn water falls into the still ים הגדול, immersing at that spot does not work, though in a flowing river there is no problem. A ברייתא supports this and adds that a loaf of תרומה falling there becomes טמא, even though it started out pure. Finally, a new משנה begins about עדים זוממין. רבי מאיר says they can get both lashes and payment, or eighty lashes, while חכמים give only one punishment.

steps.title: The משנה's first view: wine-colored and water-colored mixtures
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא of the משנה rules on two cases. In both, slightly less than three לוגין of drawn water gets topped up by a קורטוב of another liquid. In neither case is the מקוה disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take three לוגין of water minus a קורטוב, and a קורטוב of wine falls in, so it looks like wine. If it falls into a מקוה, it does not disqualify it. The same is true if a קורטוב of milk falls in and the mixture still looks like water: it also does not disqualify the מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה that it brought in to help with רב's ruling. Here is the first opinion in that משנה, the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three full לוגין of drawn water disqualify a מקוה. In both cases here, the actual water is a little less than three לוגין, and the other liquid only fills the gap. So the תנא קמא says the מקוה stays kosher, whether the mixture looks like wine or like water.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny measure of liquid
לוֹגִים, a unit of liquid volume. Three לוגין of drawn water can disqualify a מקוה.
A ritual bath, which needs forty סאה of proper water
They did not disqualify it
Appearance; how the liquid looks

steps.confusionAlert: In both cases the water itself is less than three לוגין. The wine or milk only brings the total up to three. Don't picture three full לוגין of water here.

phrases.english: less one kortov,
phrases.notes: This continues the quote from before: three לוגין of drawn water, missing a tiny bit.

phrases.english: into which a kortov of wine fell,
and their appearance is like the appearance of wine,
and they fell into a ritual bath, they did not disqualify it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין מַיִם חָסֵר קוּרְטוֹב,
phrases.english: And likewise, three log of water less one kortov,
into which a kortov of milk fell,
and their appearance is like the appearance of water,
and they fell into a ritual bath, they did not disqualify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָסֵר קוּרְטוֹב, שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכָן קוּרְטוֹב יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה quoted at the end of the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, less than three לוגין of drawn water, topped up by wine or milk, does not disqualify a מקוה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: it all depends on how it looks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees and says that appearance decides everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: everything follows the appearance.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the משנה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives one simple test: how does the mixture look?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, a mixture that looks like wine is treated as wine, and a mixture that looks like water is treated as water. Exactly where he argues with the תנא קמא is the question the גמרא will now explore.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything goes after the appearance

steps.whyThisMatters: The earlier suggestion was that רב's ruling (a wine-colored mixture does not disqualify) follows this opinion. The next steps test that suggestion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:
Everything follows the appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing opinion in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appearance alone decides whether the liquid counts as water.

steps.title: Wasn't this already an open question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we can't simply say רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, because רב פפא was unsure about this very point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב פפא already raised this as a question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רב's ruling clearly matches רבי יוחנן בן נורי. This line sets up the dilemma that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב פפא was in doubt, then the link between רב and רבי יוחנן בן נורי is not obvious. It depends on how רב read the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised it as a question (an unsolved dilemma)

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִיבַּעְיָא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא.
phrases.english: But Rav Pappa raised this as a dilemma!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִיבַּעְיָא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that רב's ruling follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב פפא treated this as an open question, so it cannot be taken for granted.

steps.title: רב פפא's first side: רב's text said 'less a קורטוב'
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רב's version of the משנה has 'less a קורטוב' in the first case. Then רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: Maybe רב's text reads 'less a קורטוב' in the first case. Then, according to the תנא קמא, three full לוגין disqualify the מקוה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי comes to say that everything follows appearance, so a wine-colored mixture does not disqualify it. In that case, רב rules like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first half of רב פפא's dilemma. It depends on the exact wording of the משנה's first case as רב learned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first case is 'less a קורטוב,' we can infer that the תנא קמא holds three full לוגין disqualify the מקוה, even if the mixture looks like wine. רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues on that point. רב's ruling that a full three-לוג wine-colored mixture does not disqualify would then match רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
They disqualify

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa asked:
Does Rav teach 'less one kortov' in the first clause,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין, לְתַנָּא קַמָּא פָּסְלִי,
phrases.english: but three full log, according to the first tanna, disqualify it,
and Rabbi Yoḥanan comes to say:
everything follows the appearance,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אוֹמֵר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי.
phrases.english: and Rav rules like Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first possibility of רב פפא's dilemma
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רב's version of the משנה say 'less a קורטוב' in the first clause?

steps.title: רב פפא's second side: no 'less a קורטוב' in the first case
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe רב's text does not have 'less a קורטוב' in the first case. Then רבי יוחנן בן נורי only argues about the second case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps רב does not have 'less a קורטוב' in the first case. Then when רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues, he argues only about the last case…
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רב פפא's dilemma. The next step finishes this possibility by spelling out what it means for רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'less a קורטוב,' the first case is three full לוגין with wine, and even the תנא קמא says it does not disqualify. That means רבי יוחנן בן נורי's disagreement is only about the milk case. If so, רב's ruling would not need to follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; it introduces the other side of a dilemma
The last clause of the משנה
Disagrees

steps.confusionAlert: Under this reading, the תנא קמא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי agree about the wine case. The argument moves to the milk case.

phrases.english: Or perhaps Rav does not teach:
'less one kortov' in the first clause,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי – כִּי פְּלִיג,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, when he disagrees,
it is on the latter clause that he disagrees,
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the milk case, where the mixture looks like water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the other side of רב פפא's dilemma
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי's disagreement is only about the milk case

steps.title: Then רב would match everyone, not just רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: Under the second reading, רב's ruling fits all opinions. So how could רבא say רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to this reading, רב speaks according to everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second possibility from Step 5 and turns it into a problem. If the first case does not say 'less a קורטוב', then רב agrees with everyone. That would contradict רבא, who said רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues only on the second case, the first case is undisputed. רב's ruling would then be accepted by all opinions. That clashes with רבא, who tied רב's ruling to רבי יוחנן בן נורי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone; a ruling no one disagrees with

phrases.english: And רב, who said his ruling, is according to everyone?
phrases.notes: This finishes the second option. The question mark means: so how could רבא say רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out where the second reading in Step 5 leads and shows it clashes with רבא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under one possible reading, רב's ruling is undisputed. So it cannot be pinned on רבי יוחנן בן נורי alone.

steps.title: רב פפא was unsure, but רבא was sure
steps.stepSummary: The doubt belonged to רב פפא only. רבא was certain of his reading, so he could say רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב פפא it was a question; for רבא it was obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. רב פפא's doubt does not bind רבא, because רבא was clear about how to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings were only רב פפא's uncertainty. רבא held that רב's version does say 'less a קורטוב' in the first case. That puts רב with רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so רבא's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He has a question or doubt about it
It is obvious to him

phrases.english: For רב פפא it is a question,
for רבא it is obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב פָּפָּא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge first raised in Step 3 and sharpened in Step 6: רב פפא's doubt does not undercut רבא, who was sure of the first reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different sages: the doubt was one sage's, not the other's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's doubt seemed to weaken רבא's claim
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was certain of the reading that places רב with רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.whatToRemember: רבא was sure that רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. Only רב פפא had a doubt.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not know this teaching about רב's version of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I did not hear this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says this teaching is new to him. This sets up אביי's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף claims no tradition about whether 'less a קורטוב' is in רב's version. This opens the door for אביי to tell him what he himself once taught.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling passed down by tradition

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
I did not hear this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף לָא שְׁמִיעָא לִי הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story connected to the question of רב's version of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף has no memory of this teaching

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף what he once taught
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught it: רב's version lacks 'less a קורטוב' in the first case, so רב matches everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and this is what you said. רב does not have 'less a קורטוב' in the first case, רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues only on the second case, and רב speaks according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reminds רב יוסף that he once taught this himself. אביי then repeats what רב יוסף had taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's own tradition matches the second possibility from Step 5. Under it, רב's ruling is undisputed. So רבא and רב יוסף's tradition read רב's משנה differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Less a קורטוב, a tiny measure

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי יוחנן' means רבי יוחנן בן נורי from the משנה, not the אמורא רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
You said it to us,
and this is what you said to us:
that רב does not teach 'less a קורטוב' in the first case,
and רבי יוחנן disagrees only on the last case,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן בן נורי from the משנה.

phrases.english: and רב, who said his ruling, is according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ לַהּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to רב יוסף's claim in Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יוסף had a tradition on רב's version of the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב יוסף taught that the first case lacks 'less a קורטוב', so רב's ruling fits everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's tradition, recalled by אביי: רב's ruling fits everyone, because רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues only on the second case.

steps.title: A barrel of drawn water falls into the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a barrel full of drawn water falls into the ים הגדול, immersing at that spot does not work, because three לוגין of drawn water may stay together there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: if a barrel full of water fell into the ים הגדול, someone who immerses there has not had a valid immersion. We worry that the three לוגין of drawn water may stay together in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about drawn water. It applies when a whole barrel of drawn water lands in the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוגין of drawn water can disqualify a מקוה. Even in the huge sea, the barrel's water might stay bunched together at the spot where it fell. So we worry the person immersed in a spot with three לוגין of drawn water.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel
The Great Sea (the Mediterranean)
Immersion for purity
We are concerned; we take the possibility into account
Three לוגין, the amount of drawn water that can disqualify a מקוה

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
A barrel full of water
phrases.notes: He means drawn water, the kind that can disqualify a מקוה.

phrases.english: that fell into the Great Sea,
one who immerses there,
his immersion does not count.
We are concerned that the three לוגין
might be together in one place.
phrases.notes: The worry is that the barrel's water stays bunched together right where he immerses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב חָבִית מְלֵיאָה מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of רב on drawn water, brought because the sugya is already discussing his rulings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing where a barrel of drawn water fell into the sea is invalid, because three לוגין may be gathered there
steps.whyThisMatters: Even a huge body of water can be a problem if drawn water may sit undiluted at the spot where you immerse.

steps.title: Only the still sea, not a flowing river
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to the ים הגדול, whose water stands still. In an ordinary river it does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to the ים הגדול, which stands still. But an ordinary river, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב's ruling to the sea alone. If the barrel falls into an ordinary river, there is no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry depends on the water staying in place. The sea's water mostly stands still, so the drawn water can stay bunched together. A river flows, so the drawn water mixes in right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically, only in this case
Stands still; it does not flow
A river

phrases.english: And only in the Great Sea,
which stands still,
but an ordinary river, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling in Step 10 to still water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern applies only to still water like the sea, not to a flowing river
steps.whatToRemember: Drawn water that falls into still water like the sea can block immersion at that spot. In a flowing river it mixes in right away, so there is no problem.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב: a barrel of wine in the Great Sea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a barrel of wine falls into the ים הגדול, immersing there does not work, since three לוגין of drawn liquid may still be together. A loaf of תרומה that falls there is also טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: if a barrel full of wine fell into the Great Sea, a person who immerses there has not become pure. We worry that three לוגין of drawn liquid may still be together in one spot. And likewise, a loaf of תרומה that fell there is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing רב said, which supports his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב worried that three לוגין of drawn liquid stay together in the still water of the ים הגדול and spoil the טבילה. The ברייתא uses the same worry, with wine instead of water. It also adds a second case: a loaf of תרומה that falls into that spot becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawn liquid, carried by hand or in a vessel, which cannot make up a מקוה
A loaf of bread that is תרומה, the כהן's portion, which must be kept pure
And likewise; the same rule applies to a second case

steps.confusionAlert: רב spoke about a barrel of drawn water, but this ברייתא speaks about wine. The idea is the same: three לוגין of liquid that cannot purify may still be gathered in one place.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
A barrel full of wine
that fell into the Great Sea,

phrases.aramaic: הַטּוֹבֵל שָׁם – לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ טְבִילָה.
phrases.english: one who immerses there, the immersion does not count for him.
We are concerned about three לוגין of drawn liquid
that perhaps they are together in one place.
phrases.notes: Literally 'that they should not be in one place.' He means we worry they are still gathered right where he dipped.

phrases.english: And likewise, a loaf of תרומה
that fell there is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב's ruling from step 10 about the ים הגדול.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that immersing where drawn liquid fell into the ים הגדול does not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a barrel of wine that fell into the ים הגדול

steps.title: What does 'and likewise' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to add the case of the loaf of תרומה with the word 'וכן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and likewise'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new idea the loaf case teaches. It looks like the same worry as the immersion case. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine stays together in one spot, it seems obvious that it can also make a loaf טמא. So the גמרא wants to know what the extra case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the point of

phrases.english: What does 'and likewise' come to add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second clause of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea the case of the loaf of תרומה teaches beyond the immersion case

steps.title: The loaf's חזקה of purity does not save it
steps.stepSummary: You might think the loaf stays pure because of its חזקה. The ברייתא teaches that the worry about the wine is strong enough to make it טמא anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, we keep the man in his original status, which is impure. Here, we keep the תרומה in its original status, which is pure. So the ברייתא teaches us that the loaf is impure anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the loaf case teaches something new. Even an item that starts out pure becomes טמא because of this worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the immersion case the person was already טמא, so his doubtful טבילה leaves him in his old status. The loaf was pure, so its חזקה would seem to keep it pure. The ברייתא teaches that the worry about the wine staying together is strong enough to beat the loaf's חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
Keep it in its original status (חזקה)
A man, a person
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The ים הגדול is still water, so we worry that drawn liquid stays gathered there. This worry spoils a טבילה, and it even makes a pure loaf of תרומה טמא despite its חזקה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
there, keep the man in his original status,
phrases.notes: His original status is impure, since he came to immerse because he was טמא.

phrases.english: here, keep the תרומה in its original status,
so it teaches us (that the loaf is impure anyway).

steps.title: משנה: Lashes and payment for false money testimony
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses claimed someone owes two hundred זוז and were found to be זוממין. רבי מאיר says they are lashed and also pay. חכמים say anyone who pays is not lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Witnesses said, 'We testify that so-and-so owes his fellow two hundred זוז,' and they were found to be זוממין. They are lashed and they also pay, because the reason that brings them to lashes is not the same reason that brings them to payment. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: anyone who pays is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about whether עדים זוממין in a money case get two punishments, lashes and payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the lashes and the payment come from two separate sources, so both apply. חכמים hold a general rule: someone who pays money for his wrong is not also lashed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven false because other witnesses say they were somewhere else at the time
They receive lashes
They pay money

Anyone who pays is not lashed

steps.title: משנה: Eighty or forty lashes for false lashes testimony
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses claimed someone deserves forty lashes and were found to be זוממין. רבי מאיר says they get eighty lashes for two separate reasons. חכמים say only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If witnesses said, 'We testify that so-and-so deserves forty lashes,' and they were found to be זוממין, they get eighty lashes: one set because of 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor,' and one set because of 'You shall do to him as he plotted.' These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: they get only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second dispute. It asks whether witnesses who plotted to get someone lashed get double lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר counts two separate פסוקים, each bringing its own forty lashes, so the total is eighty. חכמים hold they get only forty. This matches their view in the first case that they receive only one punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The punishment of forty lashes
Do not testify falsely against your neighbor (the לאו of false witness)
As he plotted; the rule that עדים זוממין get what they tried to do to the other person

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases of the משנה, רבי מאיר gives two punishments because there are two separate sources. חכמים give only one punishment.

phrases.english: 'We testify about a man named so-and-so

because of: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor,'
and because of: 'You shall do to him as he plotted,'
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And חכמים say:
they get only forty lashes.
